decisive_items: Magnetic resonance imaging of the right shoulder and left ankle demonstrated findings consistent with osteomyelitis involving the scapula and the distal tibia
response.rationale: C1 directly extends the raw MRI evidence to specify multifocal osteomyelitis, matching the two distinct sites (scapula and distal tibia) without adding unsupported claims. R5 captures the same core diagnosis but omits the distribution modifier, making C1 more complete. R3 and R6 rely on speculative tuberculosis causation not confirmed by raw spans; R2 misattributes ankle findings to septic arthritis despite MRI showing osteomyelitis.

rejected.why: No raw span confirms tuberculous osteomyelitis; sputum studies were negative and the diagnosis was only presumed.
The raw span only mentions 'possible multidrug-resistant tuberculosis' as a test consideration, not a diagnosis.
Ankle swelling/pain is explained by osteomyelitis of the distal tibia on MRI, not septic arthritis.
